status_note: The locked Ghidra oracle records the real Architecture-owned Database graph, lazy FunctionSymbol-owned Funcdata, Database-owned ScopeLocal alias identities, two distinct attachScope failure ownership contracts, and the destructor cascade. Rugra cannot express the same input graph: its concrete Architecture has no buildDatabase implementation, FunctionSymbol has no Funcdata owner, Funcdata::new has neither Architecture nor ScopeLocal, and Scope has no Architecture/Funcdata back-reference. The Rust comparand therefore reports missing capabilities instead of manufacturing a shadow graph. Overall status is MISMATCH and no covered mapping is promoted to L3.

rugra_source.snapshot_policy: Archive only the explicit crate closure from this commit and compile the live fixture as an overlay; never read live src/*.rs and never require runtime HEAD equality.

decisive_semantics.reference_output_parameters: Architecture::buildDatabase stores the new Database in Architecture::symboltab and returns the exact registered global Scope pointer. Database::attachScope stores the incoming Scope pointer and sets its parent; FunctionSymbol::getFunction caches one Funcdata pointer; Funcdata stores the exact FunctionSymbol back-reference and exact Database-owned ScopeLocal pointer. The fixture prints only same/different/null alias classes, never pointer values. Duplicate-id attach deletes the incoming Scope before throwing, while invalid-global-name attach leaves the incoming Scope caller-owned.
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_traversal_order: Database::clearReferences recursively visits Scope::children from begin to end, both std::map<uint8,Scope*> order; ScopeInternal::~ScopeInternal walks every EntryMap then every SymbolNameTree element before Scope::~Scope walks remaining children. The sentinel destructor runs in the latter child phase and observes that FunctionSymbol::~FunctionSymbol -> Funcdata::~Funcdata -> Database::deleteScope has already detached the ScopeLocal.
decisive_semantics.counter_accumulator_lifecycle: The buildDatabase override counts invocations and requires exactly one. ScopeInternal nextUniqueId is incremented only when addSymbolInternal assigns the FunctionSymbol id; FunctionSymbol::getFunction allocates only when fd is null and reuses it thereafter. Duplicate attach does not increment or replace any registered id, and both failure cases preserve the pre-existing Database state described by their records.
decisive_semantics.sorting_comparison_keys: Database::idmap and Scope::children are keyed solely by uint8 scope id. Duplicate detection uses idmap.insert before parent attachment; the unparented duplicate's getFullName is therefore the empty string, yielding the exact message 'Duplicate scope id: '. Symbol deletion uses SymbolNameTree order; the fixture installs one FunctionSymbol so there is no unobserved equal-key tie.

analysis_options.architecture_constructor: FixtureArchitecture derives from BfdArchitecture(examples/curl, default) only to override the protected virtual buildDatabase hook; the override calls the locked Architecture::buildDatabase body exactly once and records its returned aliases. All other initialization is BfdArchitecture::init.
analysis_options.symbol_loading: readLoaderSymbols is not called. The namespace, FunctionSymbol, and Funcdata use artificial RAM addresses 0x7e120400 and 0x7e120500 after normal x86-64 spec initialization, so loader-symbol contents cannot affect the ownership records.
analysis_options.error_injection: A second non-global Scope with id 0x12040001 exercises duplicate-id RecovError after idmap.insert fails. A fresh Database receives a name-bearing root Scope to exercise invalid-global-name LowlevelError before global assignment. ProbeScope destructors distinguish callee-deleted from caller-owned incoming objects.
analysis_options.destructor_probe: The exit graph has one namespace FunctionSymbol/Funcdata/ScopeLocal plus an independent sentinel child. Architecture destruction deletes Database before prototype models/types/translator; Database deletes global; namespace ScopeInternal deletes its FunctionSymbol, which deletes Funcdata, which detaches/deletes ScopeLocal; only then Scope::~Scope deletes the sentinel. The sentinel queries its still-live parent by local name and records local_present=0.
analysis_options.rugra_projection: The Rust executable constructs only Architecture::new and Funcdata::new to observe their real empty ownership fields, then prints an explicit missing-capability inventory. It does not create Database, Scope, FunctionSymbol, or ScopeLocal lookalikes and does not normalize them into the Ghidra graph.
analysis_options.debug_macros: OPACTION_DEBUG, CPUI_DEBUG, and CPUI_STATISTICS are absent.
analysis_options.normalization: No semantic difference is normalized. Raw addresses are fixed inputs; pointer addresses are deliberately replaced by equality/null classes because allocation addresses are non-semantic. Exception categories and text, map membership, parent/back-reference identities, child counts, and destructor event order remain observable. BfdArchitecture diagnostics are captured in an in-memory stream and both comparand stderr streams must be empty.
analysis_options.random_seed: none; construction, map traversal, failure paths, and output are deterministic

bfd.include_tree_hash_scheme: sha256 of bfd-include-tree-v1 plus sorted length-prefixed basenames and file contents

build_database_graph.ghidra_oracle_observation: MATCH: one call returns the exact global registered in the new Database; Database and global both point back to the same Architecture; global is id 0, empty-named, parentless, and has no Funcdata back-reference.
build_database_graph.rugra_difference: Architecture::new leaves symboltab=None and the concrete Architecture has only an external set_symboltab seam; ArchitectureBuilder::build_database is an unimplemented trait hook.

function_scope_ownership.ghidra_oracle_observation: MATCH: namespace, FunctionSymbol, cached Funcdata, Database-resolved ScopeLocal, parent, Architecture, and FunctionSymbol back-reference alias classes all have the locked values; ScopeLocal::isGlobal=false proves the Funcdata back-reference class.
function_scope_ownership.rugra_difference: FunctionSymbol has only Symbol/consume_size/entry; Funcdata::new has arch=None and scope=None; Database/Scope and varmap ScopeLocal remain distinct value-owned models.

attach_failure_ownership.ghidra_oracle_observation: MATCH: duplicate id throws RecovError('Duplicate scope id: '), deletes the incoming unparented Scope, and retains the original; invalid global name throws LowlevelError without taking/deleting the incoming Scope and leaves globalscope null.
attach_failure_ownership.rugra_difference: Public Database::attach_scope allocates its own sequential id and overwrites into value maps; it cannot receive an explicit owned Scope pointer or reproduce either failure ownership contract.

destructor_cascade.ghidra_oracle_observation: MATCH: removing FunctionSymbol removes its mapping and synchronously deletes/detaches its ScopeLocal; full Architecture destruction enters namespace destruction, deletes FunctionSymbol/Funcdata/ScopeLocal, then deletes the sentinel child, which observes local_present=0.
destructor_cascade.rugra_difference: The split value/Arc models have no FunctionSymbol -> Funcdata -> Database-owned ScopeLocal destruction cascade to run on the same input.

remaining_branches.reason: Multiple-global-scope rejection, duplicate IDs nested below a non-global parent, findCreateScope name/id disagreement, decode-created function scopes, constructor attach failure after partial Funcdata initialization, multiple FunctionSymbols and symbol-name destructor ordering, and exception injection during nested clearReferences are outside this nine-record fixture.
